newsitem.title: GERMANY: Viag to buy majority of Goldschmidt.
newsitem.headline: Viag to buy majority of Goldschmidt.

text.p: German diversified group Viag AG said on Monday it plans to acquire a majority stake in chemicals company Th. Goldschmidt AG.

Viag said it has reached agreements to buy a 27.95 percent stake in Goldschmidt from Ruetgers AG and 10.38 percent from insurer Allianz Versicherungs AG. Viag already owns 17.91 percent of Goldschmidt. The companies involved have agreed not to disclose details of the transaction, Viag and Ruetgers said in separate mandatory statements.

Viag said that after the transactions it would have a 56.24 percent stake in Goldschmidt and would control 50.34 percent of Goldschmidt's voting capital. The transfer of the shares is still subject to approval by cartel authorities, Viag said.

Viag said Goldschmidt had opportunities to grow by coooperating with Viag's chemicals subsidiary SKW Trostberg although it had no plans to merge the two chemicals companies "in the foreseeable future."
Viag said it saw scope for cooperation particularly in the areas of silicone and tensides.
Since SKW's purchase of Master Builder Technologies last year SKW has become a world market leader for construction chemicals and has a dense global sales network, Viag said.
In addition, "interesting prospects" opened up for Goldschmidt's tensides business, Viag said.
"The aim of the majority takeover is to develop the company while retaining its own profile and to strengthen its strategic position on the world market," Viag said.
Viag's activities span the production of gas and electricity, packaging materials and chemicals as well as distribution and logistics.
